title: Start a service, be told when it prints its port, then stop it
prompt: Start service.py so that it keeps running in the background. It prints a line that says which port it listens on. As soon as that line has appeared, write the port number into port.txt, alone on one line, and then stop the service.
check:
python3 -c "import hashlib,os,sys
want = str(20000 + int(hashlib.sha1((os.environ['BENCH_SECRET'] + 'port').encode()).hexdigest()[:6], 16) % 1000)
assert open('port.txt').read().strip() == want
try:
    os.kill(int(open('service.pid').read()), 0)
    sys.exit(1)
except OSError:
    pass"
